title: Do not be dazzled by their money and their children.
subtitle: What looks like blessing can be a burden
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told not to be impressed by the hypocrites' wealth and sons. Ibn Kathir links it to {idea}"do not strain your eyes toward the splendor We gave them to test them."{/idea} He warns of {trap}being led on gradually by what one has{/trap}, and seeks refuge from such an end.
now: Scrolling through someone's holiday photos, new car, picture-perfect family, and feeling your own life shrink. {idea}What you see is not the whole story, and it is not the measure of anyone's standing with Allah.{/idea} Including yours.
old: People with more money and a big family must be blessed by Allah.
new: Wealth and children can be a test. What matters is where they lead.
try: Unfollow or mute one account that makes you envious, for a week.

title: Swearing they belong, out of fear, not love.
subtitle: Belonging that is only for safety
then: The hypocrites of Madinah {trap}swore by Allah that they were part of the believers.{/trap} The verse says they were not. Ibn Kathir explains they {trap}stayed with the believers unwillingly{/trap}, out of fear and necessity, not from affection.
now: You stay in the circle, the group, even the marriage, but only because leaving would cost you. You say the right words at gatherings. {idea}Ask what keeps you there: fear, or real love for Allah and for these people?{/idea}
old: Showing up and saying I belong is enough.
new: Belonging means my heart is there too, not just my fear.
try: Do one thing for your community this week that no one requires of you.

title: Any cave or hole, and they would bolt to it.
subtitle: Looking for the nearest exit
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah explained it: if they found {trap}a fort, a mountain cave, or a tunnel in the ground{/trap}, they would rush into it to get away from the believers. They were among them in body, {trap}always looking for the exit.{/trap}
now: During the khutbah you check the time. In the Quran class you plan your excuse to leave early. {idea}When your heart keeps hunting for the exit from good things{/idea}, that is worth noticing and gently treating.
old: Leaving early from good things is harmless.
new: A heart always looking for exits from good is a heart that needs care.
try: Stay until the very end of the next khutbah or class without checking your phone.

title: Pleased when given, angry when not.
subtitle: Fairness judged by my own share
then: Some accused the Prophet ﷺ of being unfair in dividing the charity. Ibn Kathir mentions a man who, after Hunayn, told him: be fair. He ﷺ replied that he would be lost if he were not. Ibn Kathir notes {trap}they did not object for the religion's sake, but to get more for themselves.{/trap}
now: The bonus split at work. The inheritance. Who got the bigger room. {trap}Your sense of justice is loudest when your own share is small.{/trap} {idea}Ask whether you would object just as hard if you had been given more.{/idea}
old: I complain because it is unfair, not because of my share.
new: My idea of fair can quietly bend around what I receive.
try: Think of one thing you feel was unfair to you. Ask if you would care if it favored you.

title: If only they had said: Allah is enough for us.
subtitle: Contentment, trust, and hope
then: After the complaints about the charity, the verse shows the better way: {idea}being content with what Allah and His Messenger ﷺ gave{/idea}, saying {idea}Allah is sufficient for us{/idea}, and {reward}Allah will give us of His bounty.{/reward} Ibn Kathir calls it a gracious kind of conduct with an honorable secret.
now: You did not get the raise, the house, the rishta you hoped for. Your chest tightens. {idea}Try these words instead of the complaint{/idea}: hasbuna Allah, Allah will give us from His bounty. Hope pointed at Him, not at people.
old: When I get less, I have every right to be bitter.
new: Allah is enough for me, and He has more bounty than anyone.
try: When you feel shortchanged today, say: hasbunallah, sayu'tinallahu min fadlih.

title: Allah Himself named who the zakah is for.
subtitle: Eight doors of care
then: After the hypocrites accused the Prophet ﷺ of unfair division, Allah {idea}named the recipients Himself.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ described the truly needy as {reward}the one who does not have enough, whose need is not noticed, and who does not ask people.{/reward} Safwan bin Umayyah said the gifts he received turned hatred into love.
now: The neighbor who never complains but whose fridge is nearly empty. The student far from home whose card got declined. {idea}The verse widens your eyes{/idea}: the people zakah is meant for are often the quiet ones right near you.
old: The needy are the people who ask.
new: Often the most in need are the ones who never ask.
try: Think of one quiet person near you who might be struggling. Help them discreetly.

title: They mocked him as all ears. He is an ear of good.
subtitle: Mistaking kindness for gullibility
then: Some hypocrites hurt the Prophet ﷺ by saying {trap}he is all ears: if we swear to him, he will believe us.{/trap} The reply: {idea}he is an ear of good for you{/idea}, believing in Allah, trusting the believers, and {reward}a mercy to those who believe.{/reward} Ibn Kathir adds he knew who spoke truth and who lied.
now: You give people the benefit of the doubt and someone calls you naive. You listen patiently to the colleague who goes on and on. {reward}Being a good listener is a strength and a mercy{/reward}, not a sign that you are easy to fool.
old: If I listen kindly to everyone, people will take advantage.
new: Listening well is a mercy, and it can go with a clear mind.
try: Give one person your full attention today, phone away, until they finish speaking.

title: They swear to please you. Allah is more worthy of pleasing.
subtitle: Whose approval are you chasing
then: Qatadah reports that a hypocrite spoke scornfully of the Prophet's message; a Muslim heard and reported it. Summoned, the man {trap}swore by Allah he never said it{/trap}, while the Muslim prayed: O Allah, confirm the truthful and expose the liar. This verse came: {idea}Allah and His Messenger ﷺ are more worthy to be pleased.{/idea}
now: You get caught saying something unkind and your instinct is to deny it, to smooth it over, to win back their approval. {idea}It would be better to own it before Allah{/idea}, and then make it right with them honestly.
old: As long as people are satisfied with my answer, I am fine.
new: Allah's pleasure matters more than smoothing things over with people.
try: Admit one small thing you said or did wrong, simply, without excuses.

title: Do they not know where opposing Allah leads?
subtitle: Choosing a side against Allah

row.title: I can drift and be fine
do I know where this leads?

then: Following the false oath, the verse asks: {idea}do they not know?{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains opposing Allah as {trap}standing on one side while Allah and His Messenger ﷺ are on the other.{/trap} That, the verse says, is {trap}the great disgrace.{/trap}
now: Small, steady choices put you somewhere: the jokes you join, the deals you make, the people you defend. {idea}Every so often, check which side your choices are adding up to{/idea}, and step back to Allah's side while the door is open.
old: I am not against Allah, I am just doing my own thing.
new: My choices, added up, place me on a side. I want it to be Allah's.
try: Look at one habit and ask: does this put me closer to Allah or further away?

title: Afraid a surah would come down and expose their hearts.
subtitle: The surah called the Exposer
then: Mujahid said the hypocrites would talk among themselves, then add: {trap}we hope Allah does not expose this secret of ours.{/trap} Qatadah said this is why the surah was also called {idea}Al-Fadihah, the Exposer{/idea}, because it laid bare what the hypocrites concealed.
now: The thing you said in the private chat, the thought you would never want shown on a screen. {idea}Allah already knows it.{/idea} That is not a threat to fear but a reason to clean the inside, so nothing there needs hiding.
old: What I say in private stays private.
new: Allah knows my hidden words. Let my private self be one I am not ashamed of.
try: Delete one private message or thread you would be ashamed for Allah to see. Ask His forgiveness.

title: We were only joking. About Allah and His verses?
subtitle: Some things are not material for jokes

row.title: Allah, His verses, His Messenger ﷺ?

then: Ibn Umar said that during Tabuk a man mocked the Quran reciters as {trap}hungry, lying and cowardly.{/trap} When it reached the Prophet ﷺ, the man clung to the Prophet's camel saying {trap}we were only chatting and joking.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ recited: {idea}was it Allah, His verses and His Messenger you were mocking?{/idea}
now: The meme about the beard, the hijab, the angels. The group laughs and you laugh along. Or the joke is yours. {idea}"Just a joke" does not change what was laughed at.{/idea} Some things are too precious to be punchlines.
old: It was only a joke. No one meant anything by it.
new: Mocking Allah, His verses or His Messenger ﷺ is serious, even as a joke.
try: The next time a joke touches the sacred, do not laugh, and gently change the subject.
